label: Multibus cells
info:
Reads the cell voltages the go-multibus service publishes to
/dev/shm and makes them available as a JSON message.

The service owns the module and writes the file; this flow only reads it,
so it can run alongside the service without interfering.

The file is replaced atomically (write to a temporary name, then rename),
so a read either gets the previous document or the new one in full - never
half of either. No locking or retry is needed here.

Check `valid` before using the numbers. It is `link_ok && !stale`, so a
single field tells you whether the isoSPI link is delivering fresh data.

name: parse cell 1
not valid - link down or stale
Requires the go-multibus service to be running
info:
systemctl enable --now go-multibus

The service brings the module up, configures its interfaces and polls the
cell data over USB. Without it the file is absent and the file-in node
reports an error on every tick.

If `valid` stays false, check the isoSPI link:

    gocontroll-cellmon status

`tx_frames` climbing while `rx_frames` stays put means the master is
clocking and nothing is answering.
